author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dozens of volunteers gathered at the New Hampshire State Veterans Cemetery in Boscawen on Friday for a National Day of Service marking 25 years since the September 11 attacks, according to the Concord Monitor. Participants cleaned headstones, cleared brush and worked around the cemetery grounds.

Granite United Way coordinated about 130 volunteers across four locations. In addition to the cemetery project, teams served at the New Hampshire Veterans Home in Tilton, worked with Communities for Alcohol- and Drug-free Youth in Plymouth and assembled responder-support kits on the Seacoast. The projects linked remembrance with practical assistance for veterans, first responders and community organizations.

September 11 has been federally recognized as a National Day of Service and Remembrance since 2009. Friday's work offered participants a local way to honor the nearly 3,000 people killed in the 2001 attacks while supporting institutions that serve New Hampshire residents year-round. Organizers emphasized that the anniversary can be observed not only through ceremonies, but also through acts that strengthen local communities and carry the day's lessons into the future.
dek: Granite United Way organized projects at four sites as residents observed the attacks' 25th anniversary with hands-on community work.
headline: New Hampshire volunteers mark September 11 through service
